title: Data Engineer
desc: The Data Engineer is responsible for designing, building, and maintaining the company’s data infrastructure — from raw data ingestion through to production-ready datasets that serve both operational systems and AI workloads. A core focus of this role is building a comprehensive metadata and semantic layer that clearly describes every dataset, table, and field, enabling AI systems to scan, analyze, and generate reports autonomously. This role works closely with the technical team, AI team, project team, and clients to ensure data is reliable, well-documented, and ready for both human analysis and machine consumption. Job Description: The Role Data Pipeline Development Design and build automated ETL/ELT pipelines to ingest data from multiple sources (Call Center, DMS, Social Platform, third-party APIs). Develop scheduling, monitoring, and alerting mechanisms to ensure pipeline reliability and SLA compliance. Implement incremental processing, deduplication, and change data capture (CDC) strategies for high-volume data flows. Maintain and optimize existing pipelines for performance, cost, and maintainability. Metadata & Semantic Layer Build and maintain a comprehensive metadata catalog with clear descriptions for every table and column across all datasets. Design and implement a semantic layer that defines dataset purposes, field definitions, data types, business logic, and relationships between tables. Ensure the semantic layer is structured for AI consumption — enabling AI systems to understand data context, scan datasets, perform analysis, and generate reports without manual intervention. Establish and enforce documentation standards so that every new dataset or schema change is accompanied by complete metadata. Collaborate with the AI team to validate that the semantic layer provides sufficient context for automated data exploration and insight generation. Data Quality & Governance Implement automated data quality checks at each pipeline stage: completeness, accuracy, consistency, and freshness. Build monitoring dashboards to track data health metrics and alert on anomalies or pipeline failures. Establish data lineage tracking so that downstream consumers (reports, dashboards, AI models) can trace data to its source. Collaborate with stakeholders to define data ownership, access policies, and retention rules. AI Data Infrastructure Prepare and serve datasets for AI/ML workloads: feature stores, training datasets, and inference data feeds. Collaborate with the AI team to define data requirements for model training, evaluation, and monitoring. Build and maintain data APIs or serving layers that enable AI systems to consume data in real time or near-real time. Support the AI team in data profiling, exploratory analysis, and data readiness assessments for new AI use cases. Cross-team Collaboration Work with the technical team on system integration and data flow architecture across platforms. Collaborate with the AI team to ensure data infrastructure meets the requirements of AI/ML workloads. Support the project team and clients in understanding data availability, structure, and operational workflows. Participate in client-facing discussions to gather data requirements and provide technical guidance on data solutions. Job Description The Team Cola is part of GM’s autonomous vehicle effort, focused on helping teams discover, understand, and curate high-value data from large-scale real-world sensor streams. The team sits at the intersection of machine learning, data infrastructure, and developer productivity, building systems that make it easier to search for important scenarios, prepare training-ready data, and support fast iteration across perception and evaluation workflows. Our goal is to make world understanding scalable, practical, and cost efficient for embodied AI systems. We believe the next generation of autonomy and robotics depends not only on stronger models, but also on better infrastructure for turning massive volumes of multimodal data into reusable signals, searchable artifacts, and high-quality evaluation loops. That means building systems that can operate at industrial scale while preserving the flexibility to adapt quickly to new questions, new edge cases, and new model capabilities. JOB DESCRIPTION AND POSITION REQUIREMENTS The Wee Lab in the Department of Food Science, Penn State – University Park is looking for undergraduate researchers in food mycology beginning as soon as able. Projects in our laboratory center around fungal biology and mycology within the context of food and biomaterials. Responsibilities and Expectations : Undergraduate research assistants in our team typically commit 8-10 hours/week during the Spring/Fall and 30-40 hours/week during Summer. Employment is based on availability of funding and performance. Undergraduate research responsibilities include but are not limited to: General: Conduct organized research in the area of food microbiology focused on food-associated fungi; perform independent literature searches and prepare summaries of topics pertinent to ongoing and future research; prepare summaries of research projects conducted in the laboratory; conduct research under the direction of the PI leading to peer reviewed publication Research-based laboratory: perform analytical procedures and protocols as directed; collect and analyze data from ongoing research projects Microbiology: Preparation of growth media, growth of fungi, spore stock preparation Molecular biology: DNA extraction, gel electrophoresis, Sanger sequencing Basic microscopy Data management: maintain files (electronic) of protocols (assure students provide appropriately formatted and referenced protocols as they are developed) for the laboratory Laboratory safety and maintenance: conduct and comply with general laboratory safety and housekeeping; collaborate with postdoctoral associate, technicians, graduate, and/or senior undergraduate researcher No animal or work in humans Skills and Qualifications: Self-motivation, strong leadership skills, and a high level of responsibility to complete tasks in a timely manner Strong verbal and written communication skills Background in microbiology and/or food microbiology preferred Undergraduates with previous research skills encouraged to apply Ability to learn new research techniques as needed Flexibility in adjusting to new work-related requirements Maintain a grade of “B” or better in required coursework (CGPA: minimum 3.2) Strong computer skills especially with Microsoft Office, internet, and electronic media Please include a cover letter and resume with your application in WorkDay.
